event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EPAM’s 2022 Form 10-K (filed 24-Feb-2023) provides a concentrated discussion of COVID-19 as both an historic and continuing source of financial and operational risk.  The company discloses that it has already experienced negative effects on revenue, profitability and share-price volatility, while also warning that future impacts could be “material” but remain difficult to quantify because of unknown macro variables (inflation, supply-chain health, travel restrictions, client bankruptcies, labour availability, etc.).  These statements are direct, specific to COVID-19, and reference multiple impact channels—customer demand, service delivery, information-security exposure created by remote work, and cascading effects on other risk factors—demonstrating that the threat is not merely hypothetical.  Although EPAM highlights certain mitigations (e.g., large-scale shift to secure remote work that continues to operate “productively”), those remarks are outweighed by repeated acknowledgements of ongoing uncertainty and potential material adverse consequences.  Given the filing date is less than three years after the WHO pandemic declaration, Time-Decay no longer dampens severity; high—but not maximal—scores (typically 6-8) are therefore appropriate, with modest downward adjustments where the company cites concrete mitigating actions.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations have been adversely affected and could in the future be materially adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Admits past adverse impact already realised.
Projects future ‘material’ adverse impact (strong language).
Direct, event-specific reference (COVID-19).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear statement of both realised and potentially material future harm from COVID-19 justifies a high score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has contributed to significant volatility in the price of our common stock, created uncertainty in customer demand for, and ability to supply, our services and caused widespread economic disruption.

components.reason: Links COVID-19 to stock-price volatility (capital-markets impact).
Identifies reduced/uncertain customer demand.
Identifies supply-side service-delivery uncertainty.
Uses strong phrase ‘widespread economic disruption’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Multiple concrete impact channels (market, demand, supply) elevate the severity to 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the coronavirus pandemic will continue to impact our business, operations and financial results will depend on numerous factors that are unknown and that we may not be able to accurately predict.

components.reason: Acknowledges ongoing, forward-looking uncertainty tied to COVID-19.
Highlights inability to predict, increasing risk perception.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Expresses uncertainty rather than concrete impact, producing a moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Those factors include: the impact of the pandemic on economic activity, supply chains, and inflation; any interventions or government measures intended to mitigate economic and supply disruptions; our ability to sell and provide our products, services, and solutions, including as a result of travel restrictions and personnel availability; and bankruptcy or other insolvency procedures among our customers or suppliers.

components.reason: Explicitly lists macroeconomic channels (economic activity, supply chains, inflation).
Cites travel restrictions and labour shortages affecting service delivery.
Mentions potential customer/supplier bankruptcies (credit risk).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates several concrete forward-looking risk drivers but without quantification, yielding a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Broad disruptions in our customers’ markets have disrupted and could continue to disrupt the demand for our products, services, and solutions and result in, among other things, termination of customer contracts, delays or interruptions in the performance of contracts, losses of revenues, reduced profitability, and an increase in bad debt expense.

components.reason: States current disruption to customer demand already occurring.
Foresees continued disruption going forward.
Enumerates multiple concrete financial consequences (terminations, revenue loss, bad debt).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines realised impact with detailed potential financial damages, matching a high score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Remote working arrangements increase information security, cyber security and connectivity vulnerabilities and new coronavirus variants could affect our ability to deliver services to our customers because of an outbreak of illness among our employees, our customers’ employees, or at a facility.

components.reason: Identifies heightened cyber and connectivity vulnerabilities caused by remote work.
Highlights risk of service-delivery interruption from new variants and illness.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational vulnerabilities are flagged, but without financial quantification; risk assessed at 4.

evidence_list.snippet: To the extent the COVID-19 pandemic adversely affects our business and financial results, it may also have the effect of heightening many of the other risks described in this section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022, each of which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or stock price.

components.reason: Acknowledges compounding effect—COVID-19 can amplify other material risks.
Uses ‘materially adversely affect’ language, signalling severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights risk amplification but remains general; moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: To ensure safety and business continuity in the environment introduced by the COVID-19 global pandemic, many of our personnel have worked and continue to work productively through secure remote working arrangements so they can respond to the rapidly changing needs and demands of our customers.

components.reason: Describes successful mitigation (secure, productive remote-work model).
Emphasises business continuity despite pandemic conditions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Represents a clear mitigating measure, so points are negative, producing a net score of –3 (risk-reducing).

evidence_list.snippet: Our crisis management procedures, business continuity plans, and disaster recovery capabilities may not be effective at preventing or mitigating the effects of prolonged or multiple crises, such as civil unrest, military conflict, energy instability and a pandemic in a concentrated geographic area or in multiple geographies.

components.reason: Admits potential ineffectiveness of contingency plans for pandemics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but still acknowledges weakness of preparedness for pandemics, warranting a low-to-moderate score of 2.
